articles.title: The Profiler We Weren't Allowed to Have: 72 Hours of Zero-Dependency Rust at Speed Demon 2026
articles.excerpt: One lock we didn't even know was contended cost us 8.6 milliseconds — on a track whose entire run, by the end, was 27. That's close to a third of our whole budget, hiding behind a registry that looked…
articles.body: One lock we didn't even know was contended cost us 8.6 milliseconds — on a track whose entire run, by the end, was 27. That's close to a third of our whole budget, hiding behind a registry that looked completely fine on every machine we could afford to test on, because at two threads there was nothing there to find. We only caught it the way we caught almost everything that actually mattered that weekend: by shipping the wrong answer on purpose, dozens of times, failing our own hackathon's one unforgivable rule just to get the one machine that actually judged us to tell us the truth. Speed Demon, run by Hackathon Raptors, builds your Docker image and runs it five times on one dedicated Intel box, drops the highest and lowest, and the mean is the only number that counts.

articles.title: We checked robots.txt on 1,069 top websites: who blocks AI crawlers, and who still allows ChatGPT search
articles.excerpt: Everyone has an opinion on whether websites are blocking AI crawlers. We wanted the numbers, so on 4 November 2026 we downloaded the Tranco ranking of popular domains, took the top 2,000, fetched each…
articles.body: Everyone has an opinion on whether websites are blocking AI crawlers. We wanted the numbers, so on 4 November 2026 we downloaded the Tranco ranking of popular domains, took the top 2,000, fetched each site's robots.txt, and parsed the 1,069 that gave us a usable file for rules about 13 AI crawlers. We also checked whether each site serves an llms.txt. The per-site results are in a CSV you can download . The short version About 1 in 5 sites blocks the big training crawlers: GPTBot (19.7%), ClaudeBot (18.8%) and CCBot (20.7%). 25.1% block at least one of six major training crawlers. Far fewer block the crawlers that decide whether you can appear in an AI answer: OAI-SearchBot (6.7%), Claude-SearchBot (8.1%) and PerplexityBot (11.6%). 12.3% block at least one of the three.

articles.title: How to Drain Delayed Node.js Cleanup Jobs — Rate-Limited Worker Pool
articles.excerpt: TL;DR: Put the cleanup job in a queue when preprocessing, delayed execution, and acknowledgments matter. Keep the scheduler thin: it creates a work item, and a rate-limited worker owns the expensive l…
articles.body: TL;DR: Put the cleanup job in a queue when preprocessing, delayed execution, and acknowledgments matter. Keep the scheduler thin: it creates a work item, and a rate-limited worker owns the expensive logic. For simple timers, a cron trigger is easier. For DAGs, joins, or replayable event streams, choose a workflow engine or log instead. The important boundary is not “cron versus queue” in the abstract. It is where the cleanup contract lives. A cron job should say “start the nightly sweep.” The queued message should say which partition, cutoff, and attempt to process. That split lets you tune latency without rewriting the cleanup code.

articles.title: Outlook.com Is Rejecting Mail From Domains With No DMARC Record: What Actually Changed
articles.excerpt: 550 5.7.1 Message rejected: Message lacks SPF/DKIM/DMARC Auth Records (AS9031519) That single line is the whole story, and it is now landing in the logs of small businesses that have never touched a b…
articles.body: 550 5.7.1 Message rejected: Message lacks SPF/DKIM/DMARC Auth Records (AS9031519) That single line is the whole story, and it is now landing in the logs of small businesses that have never touched a bulk-mail rule in their lives. Since November 5, 2026, Microsoft's consumer mail service — outlook.com, hotmail.com, live.com and msn.com — has been bouncing some messages from any sending domain that does not publish a DMARC record. Not just bulk senders. Not just marketers. A one-line reply from a two-person office can bounce, while the next message from the same mailbox sails through. Nobody at Microsoft announced it, and the fix is one DNS TXT record.

articles.title: Breaking the Cold Chain: Technical Breakdown of CVE-2025-41450 and Cyber-Physical OT Sabotage
articles.excerpt: When cybersecurity professionals discuss critical infrastructure threats, attention usually centers on power grids, municipal water treatment, or nuclear centrifuges. Yet in modern commercial logistic…
articles.body: When cybersecurity professionals discuss critical infrastructure threats, attention usually centers on power grids, municipal water treatment, or nuclear centrifuges. Yet in modern commercial logistics, cold-chain refrigeration represents an equally critical, high-impact cyber-physical attack surface. In October 2026, a cyber-physical sabotage campaign dubbed "Fromagegate" targeted over 700 commercial supermarkets across Europe. Threat actors didn't deploy financial extortion ransomware or exfiltrate databases. Instead, they weaponized exposed Operational Technology (OT) controllers—specifically the Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA Series System Managers —to remotely trigger continuous defrost cycles, pushing temperatures in industrial freezers up to +50°C and causing millions in spoiled inventory.

articles.body: NASA’s two ESCAPADE (Escape and Plasma Acceleration and Dynamics Explorers) spacecraft have each successfully completed a powered Earth flyby, using Earth’s gravity in combination with a sustained engine burn to slingshot themselves toward Mars. articles.body: This week, as countries meet in Antalya, Turkey for the United Nations climate conference, one topic likely to dominate the conversation is artificial intelligence. The host has already called on countries to commit to ensuring that AI is designed, powered, and deployed in ways that support climate action. But so far, industries around the world aren’t doing nearly enough to harness the technology to actually drive down the greenhouse-gas emissions heating up the planet, despite some very optimistic claims from AI companies.
